summary: The acceptance candidate correctly separates most morphology warnings from technical failures, avoids WT-reference scoring in comparative tuning, uses specimen-level reporting, and labels repeated-2D-ROI volume appropriately. However, production tracking still imposes a hard 20 um reconstructed-length join veto. Length alone can therefore fragment genuine nuclei above 20 um, contradicting the claimed morphology-neutral tracking semantics and the design rule that length above 20 um is insufficient for technical intervention. This blocks biological-validity acceptance.

findings.title: Comparative tracking uses phenotype length as a hard technical veto above 20 um
findings.impact: A genuine nucleus whose reconstructed length exceeds 20 um can be split into multiple tracks even when spatial, overlap, orientation, and learned support are compatible. Source detections remain present, but fragmentation changes nucleus counts, track-level length and Z-span, and specimen summaries in a morphology-dependent way. This contradicts the claim that plausible long mutant morphology remains measurable and that global tracking is morphology-neutral.
evidence: production_profiles/saturn_v5_7_1_model_c_epoch003.json:197 sets UNET_TRACK_MAX_RECONSTRUCTED_LENGTH_UM to 20.0.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:4883-4895 selects that threshold specifically for comparative U-Net-primary tracking.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:4930-4942 rejects an otherwise proposed extension solely for exceeding the length threshold.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:5836-5846 repeats the length-only rejection in global assignment.
audits/V5_7_1_DESIGN_DECISIONS.md:13-16 states that length above 20 um is insufficient for deletion or splitting and requires objective fusion or merge evidence.
findings.recommendation: Remove reconstructed biological length as a standalone comparative tracking veto. Reject joins using objective multi-object or impossible-motion evidence, retain supported long tracks with morphology warnings, and add adversarial tests for compatible tracks crossing 20 um without objective fusion evidence.

findings.title: Automated morphology coverage does not validate the production model against biological ground truth
findings.impact: Synthetic masks establish code semantics but cannot show that the trained foreground/core heads preserve genuine fragmented-looking, fused-looking, or extreme mutant nuclei in microscopy data. Production readiness remains dependent on external biological validation of manual masks from independent specimens.

findings.recommendation: Before making biological sensitivity or phenotype-preservation claims, evaluate blinded manual instance masks from multiple independent WT and mutant specimens, stratified by short, long, wide, thin, curved, fragmented-looking, fused-looking, single-slice, and low-ratio morphology.
